stories.headline: India pledges help to rebuild school in flood-ravaged Nepal
stories.title: India pledges help to rebuild school in flood-ravaged Nepal
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: TRISHULI BAZAAR (NUWAKOT, NEPAL): India assured support for complete reconstruction of flood-ravaged Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in Bidur, two days after TOI reported that the institution was seeking New Delhi's help to rebuild on higher, safer ground.

The assurance came less than a week after around 900 students on campus escaped the Aug 26 flash flood following an emergency evacuation, while hundreds more travelling to school were stopped from entering the danger zone.
The school had 1,643 students enrolled.
Indian ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava met the school's principal Rajendra Dawadi Tuesday.
Srivastava recalled the institution's long association with India, including construction of its newer building through Indian grant assistance.
He said Dawadi's timely action had saved lives of over 1,600 schoolchildren.
TOI had earlier reported how around 900 students were inside the school when warnings came, while buses carrying hundreds of others were stopped before reaching the danger zone.
Dawadi told TOI after the meeting with Srivastava on Wednesday: "We are deeply grateful to India for the reassurance and for standing with us at this difficult time.
The assurance has given the entire school community hope at a time when we are trying to restart classes and also looking for a safe location for a permanent campus.

Our entire school infrastructure has been destroyed, so our immediate priority is to bring the students back to classrooms." The flood has swept away virtually the entire campus, including its 18-room, three-storey academic block.
The school's two buses were among the few assets left.
Two staffers - non-teaching employee Chulrim Lama and secondary teacher Santos Parihar - still remain missing.

stories.headline: Maha Kumbh, SIR: Inside RaGa's Nashik visit
stories.title: Maha Kumbh, SIR: Inside RaGa's Nashik visit
stories.summary: Mumbai: Alleged corruption in the Nashik Kumbh mela and land acquisition for the ambitious ₹1 lakh crore Shakti Peeth expressway may become part of national political discourse, with Maharashtra Congress leaders apprising Rahul Gandhi about these issues on Wednesday. Gandhi was in Nashik to address leaders at the conclusion of Maharashtra Congress' 10-day organisational training camp."There has been a lot of corruption in the infrastructure works taken up during the Nashik Kumbh mela. We spoke to him about how there is no project report for the Kumbh mela and people were not taken into confidence. The entire project seems to be to get contracts for some chosen contractors and get 40% commission," senior Congress leader Prithviraj Chavan said after the meeting.Also Read: Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027: Maharashtra government approves Rs 2,267 crore to acquire 191.21 acres of landHe said that leaders also apprised him about farmer distress and farmers' opposition to land acquisition for the Shakti Peeth Expressway. They also updated him on the SIR exercise in the state which has deleted 2 crore voters from the list. Gandhi on Tuesday took to social media and asked: "Maharashtra 2024: Suddenly 3.9 million voters were added between the Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha elections. I said it then and I say it today. This was vote theft... And now in Maharashtra, 2.07 crore voters have been removed from the draft list - that's every fifth voter. Which list was correct," he asked."BJP and the 'Vote Theft Commission' keep changing their tactics and they will continue to do so - the goal remains just one: BJP's victory at any cost, and the end of India's democracy," he added.Congress in Maharashtra has got a second wind after the recent students' protests and Gandhi's visit to Pune last month, where he highlighted issues pertaining to tribal students in the state which forced the state government to negotiate with tribal students to accept their demands.Also Read: 'Holistic' preparations underway for Nashik Kumbh Mela but it's a race against time, say authoritiesBJP carried out protests in Nashik against Rahul Gandhi, claiming Congress was against women's reservation. BJP spokesman Navnath Ban asked why Gandhi had not taken action against a Congress leader in whose ashram school in Gadchiroli three girl students died of snake bite last month.

stories.headline: Supreme Court directs Tamil Nadu to formulate rules for fishing vessel transit to Exclusive Economic Zones
stories.title: Supreme Court directs Tamil Nadu to formulate rules for fishing vessel transit to Exclusive Economic Zones
stories.summary: The court urges Union-Tamil Nadu coordination on purse seine fishing in Exclusive Economic Zones
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Urging co-operative federalism between the Centre and the State to regulate purse seine fishing, the Supreme Court on Wednesday (September 2, 2026) directed the Tamil Nadu government to frame rules to create a “specified channel” or official navigation corridor under the Marine Fishing Regulation Rules, 2020 for transit of vessels from its territorial waters to Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ) for fishing using purse seine nets.

The direction by a Division Bench headed by Justices P.S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe was part of a judgment which considered applications concerning the rights of fishermen using purse seine nets to access the EEZ beyond the territorial waters of the State of Tamil Nadu.
The State had expressed concern in court that fishers could employ purse seine nets within the 12 nautical miles of territorial waters under the guise of fishing in the EEZ.
It would be difficult for the State to regulate such activities.

On the other hand, the fishers had argued that Tamil Nadu was invoking the 2020 Rules to prevent them from even carrying these purse seine nets to the EEZ for fishing beyond 12 nautical miles which is outside the realm of the State’s regulation.

But the court concluded that fishing within and outside the territorial waters of the State was covered by specific legislation, that is, Tamil Nadu Marine Fishing Regulation Rules, 2020, and the Central law of Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the Exclusive Economic Zone Rules (EEZ Rules), 2025.
The EEZ Rules contemplates the issuance of ‘access pass’ to fishing vessels permitted into the EEZ.

Upholding both the 2020 and 2025 Rules as well-defined, the apex court directed that the “rights and liabilities of the parties will now be governed as per the relevant laws, EEZ Rules, 2025 and the Tamil Nadu Marine Fishing Regulation Rules, 2020”.

“We now have the entire legal regime through which purse seine fishing can be regulated in the EEZ, while addressing the concerns of the State government within the territorial waters… There is no conflict between the EEZ Rules of the Union and the Marine Fishery Regulation Rules, 2020 of the State of Tamil Nadu,” the court observed.
The court said the Centre’s power to regulate fishing and fisheries beyond territorial waters under Entry 57 of List.
I of the Constitution, and the State’s authority to do the same under Entry 21 of List II were “co-equal and autonomous in each of their legislative spheres”.

With the laws to address the issue of access to EEZ for fishing using purse seine nets in place, the court said it was “necessary for the Union and the State to abide by the principle of co-operative federalism”.
